headline: UBC Rage Boils Over: Thousand-Strong March Shuts The Narrows
body:
GLMZ's Universal Basic Compensation rate has not moved in six years — still fixed at 1,200 quanta per month — and yesterday, residents of The Narrows decided they were done waiting. An estimated 1,100 citizens blocked the Ferrogate Transit junction at Sable and Ninth from 07:00 until nearly 19:00, halting twelve transit lines and costing an estimated 4 million quanta in commerce delays according to preliminary Ferrogate figures. Protest organizer Declan Mwangi-Osei told reporters the crowd would return daily until the Federal Remnant's UBC Review Board convened an emergency session. 'You cannot eat a promise,' he said. 'And you cannot live on 1,200 quanta in this city. Not anymore.'

Informal surveys conducted by The Collective suggest the average cost of a single room in The Narrows now sits at 890 quanta per month, leaving residents fewer than 310 quanta for food, medical, and transit. Three protesters were treated for heat exposure on-site; a field medic from The Collective's mutual aid network ran triage from a folding table on the corner of Ninth and Crane. Ironclad security contractors were visible at the perimeter but did not move on the crowd.

The Federal Remnant's UBC Review Board issued a statement at 16:40 calling the protest 'understandable but premature,' citing an ongoing cost-of-living assessment scheduled for completion in Q1 of 2164. Declan Mwangi-Osei read the statement aloud to the crowd through a handheld amp. The crowd responded with Iron Choir singing that reportedly carried six blocks.
aftermath: The Review Board convened its emergency session twelve days later under sustained pressure, ultimately approving a 180 quanta increase — less than a third of what organizers demanded — triggering a second wave of protests in early 2164.
runner_relevance: The protests created steady courier work moving encrypted communications between organizer cells after Ironclad began monitoring open BCI channels. The Collective posted protection contracts for high-profile speakers following credible harassment threats, and Graycloaks paid runners to pull surveillance footage from Ferrogate Transit nodes to document Ironclad's perimeter activity for legal proceedings.
